question: Does the selected four-lever package satisfy the unchanged balance contract when the winning-path diagnostic recognizes top lanes within one action/resource point as a stable hybrid rather than requiring an exact tie?

diagnosticCorrection.rationale: One lane-score point equals one Core Action, Customer, Facility, or comparable end-state unit. The preregistered margin study found 56.70% of five-player package winner credit within this distance while the former exact-tie classifier recognized only 19.08%.

requiredDiagnostics: faction range at every supported count
action, opening, and corrected winning-path diversity
winner share and attribution by corrected path
margin telemetry by primary lane and persona
dominance, pairwise cycles, integrity, fallbacks, and forced no-ops

selectionRule.eligiblePackage: The candidate must pass every existing configuration-by-player-count balance check under the registered classifier, preserve all six factions and authored personas, and introduce no dominance or integrity failure.
selectionRule.rejectPackage: Any supported-count failure leaves the package unselected. Do not change the threshold, hybrid margin, or physical rules after observing this run.
selectionRule.interpretation: This validates a diagnostic correction and a package interaction together. It is not new causal evidence for a physical lever.
selectionRule.physicalBoundary: Even a full simulated pass requires explicit user approval and controlled physical play.

surfaceAudit.simulator: single shared winning-path classifier used by Monte Carlo and unified audit
surfaceAudit.tests: one-point hybrid, clear leader, and AGI paths covered
